title: Computably bounded changes of mind

based_on.title: Turing Degrees And The Ershov Hierarchy
based_on.pages: Section 2.1, printed p.2, Definition 2.3; countdown equivalence and the specified uniform diagonal join developed explicitly

summary: Allow a computable number of membership revisions for each input, describe this by a natural-number countdown, and construct a set outside every fixed finite change class.
abstract: A membership algorithm may revise its answer more often on a large input than on a small one. Suppose the input itself lets us compute a finite allowance for those revisions, while every sequence of guesses eventually becomes correct. Such sets are called omega-computably enumerable. A computable countdown records the same information by losing at least one unit whenever a guess changes. Complements and finite combinations preserve these input-dependent allowances. Joining the diagonal examples from all finite allowances gives a single set of this kind that has no fixed finite revision bound under any computable approximation. Even a computable allowance of one still supplies no computable deadline for the last revision.
